subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: all 49 participants had pulmonary ARDS (Table 1). obesity_subgroup: BMI not reported; obesity comorbidity in 22% (11/49), so not an obese population but not clearly non-obese — mixed_bmi. timing_subgroup: guidance began immediately after randomization (enrolment), with no interval from intubation/ICU admission/ARDS onset reported, so unclear per codebook ruling. ptp_target_subgroups: esophageal-catheter titration targeted end-expiratory PL > 0 and ≤ 2 cmH2O using absolute Pes subtraction. Mortality ranking: 28-day mortality is the only mortality timepoint reported and sets is_longest_reported_mortality.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap found. Compared against all clusters in studies/COHORTS.md: this is a single-center Brazilian trial (ten-bed respiratory medical ICU, Florianópolis, Brazil), registered at REBEC RBR-9b7jbxm, enrolled April 2018 to May 2021. No registration, enrolment window, centre, or authorship match with epvent1/epvent2 (US, NCT), mannheim_boesing (Germany, DRKS), mgh_lung_rescue (US, NCT), or angers (France). Cohort unique to this report, so cohort_id is null.
unclear_items: design.comparison_structure: although the trial randomises patients to parallel arms, all four titration methods were applied simultaneously to every patient at D0 and the Bland-Altman agreement analysis is within-patient; the schema provides no home for paired Bland-Altman contrasts (PEEP and Crs limits of agreement, e.g. -9.3 to 9.0 cmH2O and -8.5 to 11.4 mL/cmH2O) in a parallel_arms record — recorded here in general_notes.
outcomes (ventilator_settings).data[eit].value: main text reports EIT Day 0 median titrated PEEP 11 (IQR 7-13) but Table 3S reports 10 (7 - 13) for the same column.
population.baseline_by_arm[best_compliance].age: Table 1 reports best-compliance age as '44 (3 - 49)'; lower IQR bound of 3 years is almost certainly a typographical error (likely 39).
Supplementary Table 2S catheter-arm PaO2 d0-d3 reports '115 (88 - 12)'; upper bound 12 is a typographical error. Not extracted as an outcome.
Table 3S column headers read (n = 49) for all four methods but the row gives per-method n of 48, 46, 46, 49; header n appears to be an error.
Table 1 PEEP table-arm baseline PEEP is 10 (10 - 10.5) but Table 2S baseline PEEP for the same arm reads 11 (10 - 15); minor inconsistency between tables.

population.n_neuromuscular_blockade: neuromuscular blockade given to all patients during titration per protocol but no count/duration at baseline reported; duration of neuromuscular blocking agents reported only as exploratory outcome (Table 4S).
ventilator_free_days definition (window and death handling) not stated in the paper; definition_verbatim left null.
feasibility.n_placement_successful: all patients received a catheter but explicit placement success count is not stated; catheter loss occurred in 2 patients on D2.
data_only_in_figure: Mean respiratory system compliance evolution from baseline through Day 3 (Figure 2) — per-day arm means shown graphically; only Day 0 values given in text
Mean titrated PEEP values from baseline through Day 3 (Figure 3) — per-day means shown graphically with some point labels
extraction_flags.general_notes: Within-patient agreement analyses (Bland-Altman, six pairwise contrasts for titrated PEEP and six for derived Crs across the four methods, n=49 each) are reported in text, Figure 4, Figure 5 and Section 8S. Example verbatim: 'PEEP titrated by PEEP/FiO2 table was 0.1cmH2O lower than PEEP titrated by the catheter with limits of agreement from -9.3 to 9.0cmH2O'. These have no schema slot in a parallel_arms record; flagged in unclear_items. Pearson correlations between methods also reported (PEEP: catheter vs EIT r=0.34; catheter vs best compliance r=0.33; catheter vs table r=0.13; best compliance vs EIT r=0.84; table vs EIT r=0.54; table vs best compliance r=0.58; Crs from titrated PEEP all strong, Figure 8S).
